soil_drainage — removed on audit: Value is "moderate", but no admissible source uses that word or anything like it, and the sources actually describe two SEPARATE properties that the researcher averaged together. The PSU quote cited says "soils that are not compacted, have good drainage, and hold moisture well" -- "good drainage" is the drainage-rate statement, "hold moisture well" is a separate moisture-retention statement (already captured by water_regime=keep_moist). I fetched NC State's live asparagus page directly and its own structured Cultural Conditions field reads "Soil Drainage: Good Drainage, Moist" -- these are two distinct checkbox entries from NC State's controlled vocabulary, not a single "moderate" rating. Folding a moisture-retention fact into the drainage field to land on a middle enum value is a category error that double-counts the moisture information and downgrades the drainage rate below what every source states (good/well-drained, not moderate). This is not a one-off judgment call: this exact codebase's own prior audits removed the identical "moderate (well-drained but moisture-holding)" pattern from at least two other species in app/data/verified/b6-core-gaps.json (lines ~563, ~1021) and app/data/verified/b5-edible-and-garden.json (line 85, in the very same batch category as this asparagus record), each time citing the same NC State "Good Drainage / Moist" two-tag structure as the tell. Failure direction: a soil recommended as merely 'moderate' drainage steers a grower toward a heavier, slower-draining bed mix than an extension-recommended free-draining bed for a crown crop that is notably prone to crown/root rot in wet soil.

water_growing_days_est — removed on audit: Value is 7 (labeled an estimate, built from UGA's "approximately 1 inch of water every week"), but this directly contradicts an established, audited convention in this same codebase for exactly this class of plant. Every single garden_bed record in the fully-verified b5-edible-and-garden.json batch (Tomato, Kale, Mint, Melon, Sunflower, Pumpkin, Peony, Myrtle) and every garden_bed record in b7-culinary-herbs.json leaves water_growing_days_est null, with the audited rationale stated explicitly in the Tomato record's unknowns: "in-ground garden crop, so interval is driven by weather and soil, not a pot/medium assumption we can state. water_regime carries the real fact." Failure direction: a user who waters on a rigid 7-day timer regardless of actual rainfall over-waters during wet stretches (risking the crown/root rot asparagus is prone to in slow-draining or waterlogged soil) and under-waters during dry ones.
